overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to keep minutes for many years and by not posting topic lists in its meeting notices, and ordered compliance, training, and minute reconstruction.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission has not created and maintained minutes for most of its meetings over the past twenty years.
allegations.key_passage: we find that it failed to create and maintain meeting minutes for many years prior to the filing of this complaint in August 2021, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission has not posted meeting notices containing a list of topics to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: We also find that the Commission did not post notice of each meeting containing a listing of topics that the chair reasonably anticipated would be discussed, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

We order all members of the Commission to attend an Open Meeting Law webinar training provided by our office within 90 days of the date of this letter and to certify to our office that they have done so.
Within 90 days of receipt of this letter, the Commission shall certify to our office that it has complied with this order to create meeting minutes.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law and may result in the imposition of a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per intentional violation.
